reviewBoundary: Three new complete senior clozes. Fictional astronomy, collaborative pottery and oral-history scenarios. Same-author context and all-alternative review, with no independent teacher/student calibration claimed.

units.title: The cloud over Saturn
units.alignmentNote: One complete original fifteen-gap four-choice narrative, following National I final structure. Old source is a level/family reference only.

materials.title: The cloud over Saturn
materials.text:
I volunteered at a public astronomy evening because I wanted to show people Saturn. Having seen its rings, I wanted to share the ____1____. Experienced observers supervised our telescopes on the school field.

Just as the first family arrived, a broad cloud covered the part of the sky we needed. I kept looking up, hoping it would ____2____. The queue grew while our telescope showed nothing useful.

My supervisor, Helen, asked me to talk to the visitors. I began apologising for the ____3____. She smiled and asked a child what he expected Saturn to look like. He spread his hands wide. "Huge!"

Helen showed him the small circle on our information card. Through this telescope, the planet would look ____4____, not like the large photographs in a book. The child moved closer to examine the drawing.

Other visitors joined the conversation. Someone asked why the rings would appear tilted.  While we spoke, the queue became less like a line of ____5____ customers and more like a group with questions.

The cloud eventually moved. We invited people to look in ____6____. Some needed help finding the tiny image. One woman said the view was smaller than she had imagined but more ____7____ because she was seeing it herself.

At closing time, I thanked Helen for rescuing the evening. She shook her head. We had not ____8____ the cloud, she said; we had used the time underneath it.

I had thought volunteering meant delivering a perfect ____9____. Now I understood that the waiting could be part of the experience if we made room for ____10____. Not knowing every answer did not make me ____11____. I could help find someone who knew. Next time, I brought fewer promises about a clear sky and more ways to ____12____ a conversation. Saturn remained a ____13____. But I no longer treated the people waiting to see it as a ____14____ between me and the telescope. They were the reason we had brought it ____15____.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 1.
questions.explanation: The rings are a remarkable sight to share. Cost, weight and address do not describe the visual experience.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 2.
questions.explanation: The narrator hopes the obstructing cloud will move. Staying/growing would prolong obstruction; freezing is not the required change.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 3.
questions.explanation: The cloud creates a delay in viewing. Equipment is supervised and available, no journey is being apologised for, and tickets are not discussed.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 4.
questions.explanation: The card corrects the child’s expectation of huge: the telescopic image is small. Colourlessness and familiarity are not the contrast.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 5.
questions.explanation: A growing queue waiting without a useful view risks impatience; conversation turns waiting into participation. Invisibility and wealth are irrelevant, and the group was not described as unable to speak.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 6.
questions.explanation: In turn means one after another at a telescope. In secret conceals, in advance is beforehand and in danger is unsafe.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 7.
questions.explanation: Seeing it personally makes the view exciting despite small size. Price and distance do not express the visitor’s new engagement; ordinary diminishes it.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 8.
questions.explanation: They cannot remove the cloud; they use the waiting time. Predicting, photographing and following were not the claimed rescue actions.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 9.
questions.explanation: The volunteer initially aims to supply a perfect telescope view. Meal, map and score do not name the planned service.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 10.
questions.explanation: The successful wait contains visitors’ questions and shared explanation. Complaint, sales and silence are not its productive change.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 11.
questions.explanation: Not knowing everything does not remove the volunteer’s usefulness; seeking help is valuable. Fame, hunger and lateness are unrelated to knowledge limits.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 12.
questions.explanation: Bringing ways to start a conversation prepares engagement during waiting. Avoiding or ending reverses it, and copying does not express initiating one.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 13.
questions.explanation: Saturn remains the special attraction, a highlight. It is neither a mistake nor secret, and the narrator stops promising clear skies rather than treating the planet as a promise.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 14.
questions.explanation: The final insight stops viewing visitors as a barrier to personal telescope access. Bridge and gift are positive links, while conversation is the new means rather than an obstruction.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 15.
questions.explanation: The telescope is set up outside in the school field. Upstairs, indoors and home contradict the stated public setting.

units.title: The cup nobody could finish alone

materials.title: The cup nobody could finish alone
materials.text:
In pottery class, each student began a cup. After ten minutes, the unfinished work moved one place left. I looked at the clay in front of me with some ____1____. I had a clear idea, and now somebody else would change it.

I shaped a tall cup with a narrow base. When the signal sounded, I passed it to Ben and received a wide, uneven bowl. My first impulse was to ____2____ it into the cup I had intended. Then I noticed two small marks where its maker had begun a handle.

I asked the teacher whether we could consult the previous person. She welcomed a brief ____3____, rather than orders. Its maker wanted something easy to hold with both hands.

That changed my ____4____. Instead of forcing it taller, I strengthened its sides and smoothed the rim. Then it moved on again.

At the final stage, I received a cup with a beautifully simple handle. I wanted to add decoration but could see that the plain surface was part of its ____5____. I cleaned the base and left the rest alone.

Before firing, we examined all the pieces. My original tall cup had become shorter and ____6____. Ben explained that the narrow base had made it unstable. Another student had added a handle.

I could still recognise my starting shape, but it no longer belonged only to my ____7____. I would not have made every change, but understood their ____8____.

The teacher asked what had been hardest. "Knowing when not to add something," I said. Collaboration had not meant leaving a visible ____9____ on every object. Sometimes it meant making a joint decision, sometimes noticing a weakness, and sometimes showing ____10____. I became more interested in what another intention made ____11____. The cups were imperfect, but each carried a series of ____12____ rather than one uninterrupted command. After firing, I no longer asked which one was ____13____. We asked who had done what, and listened to the ____14____ of how a handful of clay had passed through so many ____15____.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 1.
questions.explanation: The narrator resists others changing a clear private plan, indicating reluctance. Excitement, relief and confidence do not match that concern.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 2.
questions.explanation: The impulse is to reshape the received bowl into the originally planned cup. Sale, concealment and firing do not transform it to that design.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 3.
questions.explanation: A brief conversation lets the prior maker explain without commands. Competition and silence do not exchange intentions; lecture implies one-way delivery rather than consultation.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 4.
questions.explanation: Understanding intended two-handed use changes the design approach. Price, timetable and seat are not what the explanation alters.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 5.
questions.explanation: The plain surface is part of its appeal, so decoration may undermine it. Weight, owner and damage do not name the attractive simplicity.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 6.
questions.explanation: The initially narrow base is made wider to improve stability while the cup becomes shorter. Taller and narrower reverse those adjustments; colder is not the geometric repair.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 7.
questions.explanation: Others’ changes move it beyond the narrator’s original imagination. The teacher and kiln are not the private source of design, and class is the new shared context.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 8.
questions.explanation: The explained changes improve stability and handling, making their purpose understandable. Cost, popularity and speed are not the reasons given.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 9.
questions.explanation: Leaving a visible mark means showing a contribution, contrasted with restraint. Price is commercial, flaw is a defect, and shadow a light effect rather than a contribution.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 10.
questions.explanation: Cleaning without unnecessary decoration demonstrates restraint. Anger, confusion and haste are not that deliberate decision.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 11.
questions.explanation: Another intention opens different possible designs. Expense, secrecy and identity are not the creative opportunity.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 12.
questions.explanation: Successive makers respond to earlier work rather than obey one command. Orders repeats the rejected model, while accidents and prizes do not describe the deliberate exchanges.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 13.
questions.explanation: The shift from individual ownership to shared contributions means they no longer ask which cup is mine. Emptiness, breakage and size are not the ownership question.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 14.
questions.explanation: They listen to the story of each cup’s making. Sound is not the account itself, price financial and rule prescriptive.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 15.
questions.explanation: Passing through hands represents the several makers. Shops, fires and shelves are not the sequence of people in class.

materials.title: The laugh between the answers
materials.text:
I interviewed a retired baker, preparing questions about hours, wages and methods. During the conversation, however, she kept returning to a ____1____: the sound of her colleague laughing before dawn.

I steered us back to my list. The laughter seemed like an attractive ____2____, not the substance of the interview. When I listened to the recording later, my own interruptions embarrassed me.

Her voice changed when she recalled that colleague. The memory explained why she had stayed in a demanding job. Without it, the early starts and heavy trays described the ____3____ but not her experience of it.

I asked whether I could return for a shorter conversation. This time, I began with the colleague. The baker described jokes exchanged while dough was rising and the relief of having someone who noticed when she was ____4____. Her account made the support visible.

While editing, I faced another temptation. A long pause followed one answer, and I wanted to ____5____ it to keep the pace lively. She had been deciding how to describe a difficult farewell. Removing the pause would make the words sound more ____6____ than they had been.

I kept some of the silence and checked the excerpt with her. She approved it, asking only that we correct the ____7____ of a street: one letter was missing. Accuracy still mattered.

The finished piece contained fewer of my planned facts but more of her ____8____. I had not abandoned preparation; I had learned to let it ____9____ rather than dominate. An interview was not a container for my expected information. It was an ____10____ in which another person chose what to share.

Beside later question lists, I left a ____11____ space. It reminded me that the most useful follow-up might come from something I had not ____12____. The baker's laugh had been easy to classify as a digression. Taking it ____13____ had led me closer to the working life I wanted to understand. Now I tried to listen for the meaning ____14____ a detail before deciding whether it belonged ____15____ the final account.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 1.
questions.explanation: The remembered colleague’s laugh is a memory. A price, recipe and deadline do not name that recollection.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 2.
questions.explanation: The interviewer initially regards it as a digression from the prepared factual list. Discovery implies central new information, instruction a direction and argument a dispute.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 3.
questions.explanation: Hours and heavy trays describe working conditions rather than lived meaning. Future, audience and purpose are not the physical demands listed.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 4.
questions.explanation: A supportive colleague notices difficulty, or struggling. Fame, absence and promotion do not express the need for relief described.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 5.
questions.explanation: Editing for lively pace tempts cutting a pause. Repeating lengthens it, measuring assesses duration and translating is not the silence problem.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 6.
questions.explanation: The pause marks a difficult decision; removing it would falsely make the farewell sound casual. Distance, privacy and accuracy do not express reduced emotional deliberation.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 7.
questions.explanation: The missing letter establishes that the street name needs correction. Direction, length and location do not consist of a misspelt identifying word.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 8.
questions.explanation: Voice represents her perspective and expression, now more present than the interviewer’s planned facts. Income, equipment and schedule are the former factual focus.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 9.
questions.explanation: Preparation should guide rather than dominate. Vanishing abandons it, entertainment is not its interviewing function and interruption was the initial mistake.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 10.
questions.explanation: An interview is a conversational exchange with another person choosing what to share. Inspection, advertisement and experiment do not describe that reciprocal account.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 11.
questions.explanation: A deliberately blank space symbolises openness to unplanned follow-ups. Crowded/finished oppose that, and narrow does not establish emptiness.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 12.
questions.explanation: The blank area welcomes something unanticipated. Heard is inevitable in a follow-up, forgotten memory loss and written a record form, not a prior expectation.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 13.
questions.explanation: Taking the detail seriously means valuing it as evidence of experience. Personally implies offence, secretly concealment and literally a nonfigurative interpretation not at issue.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 14.
questions.explanation: Meaning behind a detail is its underlying significance. Beside, against and above do not express that interpretive relation.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 15.
questions.explanation: Belonged in the final account means had a place in that narrative. From, towards and beside do not complete this inclusion construction.
